# Read-back

This is a forty-five-minute small-group HIIT workout for three athletes rotating through four exercise stations (rower, kettlebell, box, sled) over four rounds. Each athlete works for sixty seconds at a station, then rests for sixty seconds on the floor before rotating to the next station; the rotation is fixed so that no two athletes occupy the same station in any round, and one station sits empty each round. There is exactly one piece of each equipment (one rower, one kettlebell, one box, one sled), so the constraint is that only one athlete can use each station at a time, and the hand-off is strict — the next athlete cannot start until the previous one has left. The workout opens with a five-minute warm-up all together, then runs four rounds of the rotation (60s work + 60s rest per station), and closes with a ten-minute cooldown all together after the last station is done. No explicit finish time was given; the schedule should finish as early as the work allows. The coach notes that the sled is the longest reset and most likely to bottleneck the hand-offs because it is far away.
